lead:
On the eve of Nigeria's 66th Independence anniversary, Aliko Dangote began building a $16 billion refinery in Kenya, the government declared Thursday a public holiday, and President Tinubu signed the law keeping the 2025 capital budget alive until December.

The day in brief: at Lamu Port, Dangote broke ground beside President William Ruto and Olusegun Obasanjo on a plant due for completion in 2030. Defence Headquarters said troops killed 554 suspected terrorists and criminals, arrested 1,333 and freed 1,736 hostages between July and September. In Minna, three people died in a stampede at Government House after word spread that N10,000 would be handed out, a tragedy Atiku Abubakar said no family should suffer. Twenty-nine Nigerian universities made the 2027 Times Higher Education world rankings, up from 24. Nyesom Wike promised to quit as FCT minister if Tinubu loses Rivers or the FCT, the Oyo Assembly endorsed state police, and Eric Chelle insisted the Super Eagles can still qualify for AFCON after the defeat in Bissau.

items.h: Dangote breaks ground on $16bn refinery in Kenya
items.s: Aliko Dangote performed the groundbreaking for his $16 billion Lamu refinery in northern Kenya on Wednesday, with President William Ruto, former President Olusegun Obasanjo and other African leaders in attendance. The 700,000-barrel-a-day plant is due for completion in 2030 and is meant to cut East Africa's reliance on imported fuel; Honeywell will provide engineering, licensing and equipment. Dangote said Africa must raise its own capital and build at global scale.

items.h: 1 October declared public holiday; Tinubu to address the nation
items.s: Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo announced on behalf of the Federal Government that Thursday, 1 October, is a public holiday for the 66th Independence anniversary. He congratulated Nigerians at home and abroad, said peace and stability are conditions for any nation's development, and urged citizens to follow the founding fathers' example in loving the country and working for a more united and prosperous Nigeria. The President was due to address the nation.

items.h: Tinubu signs extension of 2025 budget to December
items.s: President Tinubu signed the Appropriation (Amendment) (No. 4) Act, which moves the deadline for the capital part of the 2025 budget from 30 September to 31 December 2026, his spokesman Bayo Onanuga said. Both chambers passed it on Tuesday. During the Senate debate one senator blamed the centralised payment system for slow project execution, calling it a cork in the wheel of budget implementation.

items.h: Military says 554 terrorists killed and 1,736 hostages freed in third quarter
items.s: Defence Headquarters said troops killed 554 suspected terrorists and criminals, arrested 1,333 and rescued 1,736 hostages between July and September, in a period that saw 367 attacks across the theatres of operation. Major General Michael Onoja, director of defence media operations, said that in September alone soldiers rescued 655 kidnapped civilians and arrested 350 suspects, while 75 insurgents surrendered.

items.h: Three die in stampede at Niger Government House over N10,000 handout
items.s: Three people were killed and others hurt on Tuesday night when a crowd surged at the Niger State Government House in Minna amid reports that N10,000 would be shared. Atiku Abubakar, the ADC presidential candidate, said the dead should be remembered as people with names, families and futures. “Three Nigerians reportedly went to a Government House and did not return home,” he said, adding that no Nigerian should die seeking such a handout.

items.h: 29 Nigerian universities in THE 2027 rankings
items.s: Twenty-nine Nigerian universities appear in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings, up from 24 a year earlier. Covenant University, the University of Ibadan and the University of Lagos share the country's top band, 801 to 1,000 in the world. Osun State University entered for the first time in the 1,201 to 1,400 band, alongside Babcock and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. Oxford stayed first globally for an 11th year.

items.h: Fake council chief Adeyemi remanded in Kuje
items.s: A Federal High Court in Abuja remanded Adeniyi Adeyemi, the self-styled director-general of the Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council, at Kuje Correctional Centre after he pleaded not guilty to eight counts of conspiracy, forgery and impersonation. He was arraigned before Justice Mohammed Umar after several failed attempts to bring him to court, and after the Attorney-General of the Federation took over the prosecution.

items.h: Police defend arrest of men in #TinubuMustGo T-shirts
items.s: Police in Borno said the five men held in Maiduguri while wearing T-shirts printed “Tinubu Must Go” were found with drugs, a claim Amnesty International rejected as it demanded their release. Atiku Abubakar also called for them to be freed, saying that if a slogan was the reason for their arrest, the authorities must explain how wearing a shirt became an offence in a democracy.

items.h: Wike vows to resign if Tinubu loses FCT and Rivers
items.s: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike told a mechanics' and traders' association in Apo that he would step down if President Tinubu loses the 2027 presidential vote in Rivers State or the FCT, and said his ability to deliver would justify his staying in office. “By January 17, 2027, I will announce my resignation as FCT minister should the president lose in Rivers and the FCT,” he said.

items.h: Pantami confirmed Gombe PDP governorship candidate
items.s: The PDP declared former minister Isa Ali Pantami its 2027 governorship candidate in Gombe after Tuesday's rerun primary in the state's 114 wards. He had first been affirmed in May, but a Federal High Court voided that process last week. The committee announced him the winner ahead of Usman Aliyu Garry and Khamisu Mailantarki, though the vote totals reported by different outlets did not agree.

items.h: Court voids Gombe APC House primary
items.s: Justice Vera Ibrahim of the Federal High Court in Gombe annulled the APC's 16 May primary for the Billiri/Balanga federal constituency, which had returned Ali Isa J.C., the sitting member and a former minority whip, as candidate. She ordered a fresh primary and barred him from it, finding that his name was missing from the membership register the party gave INEC, as the Electoral Act requires.

items.h: Oyo Assembly passes state police amendment
items.s: The Oyo State House of Assembly passed the Sixth Alteration Bill, which would give state police services a constitutional basis while keeping the Nigeria Police Force. Lawmakers took the bill clause by clause on Tuesday under Speaker Adebo Ogundoyin, after the Clerk of the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, sent it for their approval. Oyo follows Rivers, which voted on Monday; 24 states must concur.

items.h: Tinubu sends research fund and medical college bills to Reps
items.s: President Tinubu wrote to Speaker Tajudeen Abbas sending the Niger Delta Development Commission's 2026 budget proposal and two bills. One would create a National Research Development Fund to pull scattered research money across ministries and agencies into a single pool; the other amends the National Postgraduate Medical College Act. The NDDC budget was sent under Section 121 of the Constitution.

items.h: Chelle says AFCON hopes alive after Bissau defeat
items.s: Eric Chelle said Nigeria's hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are still alive after the 3-0 loss to Guinea-Bissau. The defeat in Bissau leaves the three-time champions on three points from two games, three behind the group leaders, after a 2-1 win over Madagascar in Uyo. Commentators compared the campaign with the one that ended Nigeria's hopes of reaching the 2026 World Cup.

items.h: Atiku repeats call to publish Nigeria-US health pact
items.s: Atiku pressed again for the full text of Nigeria's health agreement with the United States to be published, saying Ghana had turned down a similar compact over medical records, pathogen samples, funding obligations and inspection of imported medicines. “At this point, Nigerians do not know whether the provisions Ghana rejected are in the agreement Tinubu signed,” he said, urging Tinubu to follow President Mahama's example.

items.h: Ekiti APC and PDP launch joint drive for Tinubu
items.s: Ekiti Governor Biodun Oyebanji of the APC and Wole Oluyede, the PDP's candidate in the state's June 2026 governorship election, joined forces to campaign for President Tinubu's re-election. Organisers of the unusual cross-party alliance said they aim to deliver 90 per cent of Ekiti's votes to the President in 2027 and presented it as a significant boost to his bid for a second term.

items.h: Uzodimma expands media campaign; Shettima seeks northern support
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima asked northern performing artists, who visited under the Triple-R For Renewed Hope banner, to back Tinubu's re-election in the interest of fairness and national unity, and promised continued support for the region's entertainment industry. Imo governor Hope Uzodimma, meanwhile, extended his publicity network for the Renewed Hope agenda down to wards and polling units, warning that poor communication distorts how policies are seen.

items.h: FG plans 24-hour power Energy Zones
items.s: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe has begun talks with selected electricity distribution companies on dedicated Energy Zones meant to give homes, businesses and industries 24-hour supply in the busiest demand centres. The first zones would cover the Lagos axis and the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano and Enugu-Port Harcourt corridors. The ministry said the plan targets bottlenecks at the distribution end of the power chain.

items.h: CBN says recapitalisation is a starting point
items.s: CBN Deputy Governor Muhammad Sani Abdullahi told business editors and finance correspondents that the banking recapitalisation, under which 33 banks met the new minimum capital, is only a starting point. Banks must now pair bigger capital with sound governance, tighter risk management, cybersecurity and lending to the productive economy, he said, as they face geopolitical, technological and climate risks.

items.h: GTCO files audited half-year results
items.s: Guaranty Trust Holding Company filed its audited accounts for the six months to June with the Nigerian Exchange and the London Stock Exchange, reporting profit before tax of N603.03 billion. Interest income rose 7.5 per cent and trading income 24.7 per cent, but a N46.2 billion fair-value loss held growth in pre-tax profit to 0.4 per cent from a year earlier.

items.h: Wike's son submits US passport to court in land case
items.s: Jordan Wike, son of the FCT minister, presented his American passport to Justice Sylvanus Oriji of the FCT High Court, who had ordered him to produce it in a suit alleging a $2.1 million Abuja land allocation scam. Jordan, a lawyer, told the court he was abroad when the claimants say he collected the cash in Gwarimpa, that his signature on their document was forged and that he has no link with them. The case was adjourned to 1 December.

items.h: JAMB extends deadline for 2021-2025 admission offers
items.s: Candidates who were offered places between 2021 and 2025 but never responded now have until 30 November 2026, instead of 30 September, to accept or decline on JAMB's CAPS portal. The board said it granted the extra time because the system was down for about 96 hours, and told those affected to log in and act before the new date or risk losing their places.

items.h: FCTA to complete Utako hospital and upgrade 14 others
items.s: The FCT Executive Council, chaired by Minister Nyesom Wike, approved immediate renovation and upgrading of all 14 general hospitals in the territory, with new medical and diagnostic equipment and better operating theatres, and the resumption of work on the long-abandoned Utako hospital. The council also approved a new police division at Wasa, where mechanics and artisans are to be moved from Apo.

items.h: Kaduna rehabilitates 17 health centres
items.s: Kaduna is turning 17 primary health centres into centres of excellence and has given tricycle ambulances to clinics to speed emergency referrals in rural and underserved communities. The Secretary to the State Government, Abdulkadir Mu'azu Mayere, announced the work at a groundbreaking on Wednesday, describing it as part of Governor Uba Sani's push to bring quality care within reach of every resident.

items.h: Kaduna BRT to start in early 2027
items.s: Kaduna's planned bus rapid transit system is due to begin in the first quarter of 2027, said Inuwa Ibrahim, managing director of Kaduna Line. The first phase covers 17 kilometres with 20 stations, a terminal at Kawo, a depot and dedicated lanes. “We are looking at creating 10,000 to 20,000 jobs,” he said, mostly from running and maintaining the buses and related services.

items.h: Kano revives Goron Dutse reservoir
items.s: Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf restarted water distribution from the Goron Dutse reservoir, which had been out of use for about 30 years. The restored reservoirs and pumps are expected to add 40 million litres of drinking water to Kano metropolis's supply. The state said the rehabilitation is part of a wider effort to fix long-standing problems in producing, treating, storing and distributing water.

items.h: Yobe pays N6bn to 4,271 council retirees
items.s: Yobe has paid more than N6 billion in pensions and gratuities to 4,271 retired local government workers and the next of kin of deceased staff, said the Secretary to the State Government, Mohammed Goje. He spoke when members of the committee Governor Mai Mala Buni reconstituted in July 2022 to verify council retirees briefed him on their progress.

items.h: NSCDC deploys to Ekiti flood areas
items.s: The Ekiti command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps sent officers to flood-hit and flood-prone communities after days of heavy rain caused flooding and erosion across the state. Commandant Sotiyo Igbalawole Emmanuel ordered the deployment as part of the corps' role as a first responder in emergencies, while Governor Biodun Oyebanji sympathised with families affected by the floods.

items.h: Senate to hold two-day security summit
items.s: Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin said the Senate will host a two-day national security summit on 12 and 13 October to strengthen the country's security architecture. In his Independence message he said the National Assembly would back measures to improve security, grow the economy and raise living standards, and urged Nigerians to renew their faith in the country.

items.h: Customs returns rescued gorilla to Congo
items.s: The Nigeria Customs Service returned Bili, a female baby gorilla seized from traffickers in August 2023, to the Republic of Congo after DNA tests confirmed her origin. She was cared for by the Pandrillus Foundation in Calabar for three years and flown from Lagos to the Tchimpounga sanctuary in Pointe-Noire between 22 and 28 September, the service's first full-cycle international wildlife operation.

items.h: Retired justice warns judges against politicians' gifts
items.s: Justice Ibrahim Musa Saulawa retired from the Supreme Court at 70 and used his valedictory session to warn judges against accepting “Greek gifts” from politicians and litigants. He said gifts can be tempting, but judicial officers need contentment, integrity and honesty to rule without fear or favour. The Chief Justice described him as a man of integrity and principle.

items.h: 26MW Akute plant to power Lagos Water
items.s: Fenchurch Group began rebuilding the 26-megawatt Akute power plant to give dedicated electricity to major Lagos waterworks, which will provide about two-thirds of the state's public water capacity once Adiyan Phase II is complete. Old engines are being replaced with new gas engines; the first 10MW is expected within four months and the rest within a year, under a concession with the Lagos government.

items.h: Morocco names first woman prime minister
items.s: King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as Morocco's first woman prime minister and asked her to negotiate a coalition, after her Authenticity and Modernity Party won 97 of 395 seats in the 23 September parliamentary election. The party, founded in 2008, has positioned itself as a counterweight to the Islamist Justice and Development Party.

items.h: Flydubai co-pilot allegedly stabbed pilot mid-flight
items.s: A Flydubai Boeing 737 flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv as FZ1073 made an emergency landing at Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia after a reported fight between its two pilots, with the co-pilot alleged to have stabbed the captain. Israeli media said the jet dropped about 13,000 feet in 30 seconds and sent a signal suggesting unlawful interference; about 150 passengers were reported on board.
